relationship_S1_S2.statement: S1 cites S2 and its abstract ranges overlap S2 Tables 6.2/6.3: power 540-770 W (Runs 1,2,4-7) vs 500-800 W; S2 'global efficiency' of stable runs 0.14-0.17 vs 14-18 %; one-side Isp 1009-1146 s vs 1000-1100 s; thrust 17.29 (Run 5 averaged) - 22.79 (Run 4 one-side) mN vs 17-22 mN. S1 therefore very probably reports the same 2019-20 SPPL campaign, possibly re-reduced. Which runs and which thrust reduction S1 uses cannot be checked without S1's full text.

performance_table_6_2.uncertainty_basis: +- = maximum distance of the 3 calibration points from the best-fit line only (p.94). Excludes thermal drift, cold-gas thrust (<3 % for Xe per [54]; 'may introduce greater errors' for N2, p.111), misalignment, flow leakage, mode changes. Run 6 +-0.02 mN is a fit artefact, not a credible total uncertainty.
performance_table_6_2.reduction_ambiguity: one-side (left half of calibration pyramid, author calls conservative) vs averaged (both halves): averaged is 6-18 % lower (Runs 2/4/5/6: 1.45/2.74/3.56/4.10 mN). Analogous to the P5 divergence reading A/B; must be carried as a layer-1 reading if ever scored.
performance_table_6_2.stand: inverted pendulum (AFRL design), LVDT Macro Sensors PR 812, magnetic damper, Arduino DUE via voltage divider (p.85-88)

derived_checks.finding: Table 6.2 Isp = T/(g0 x 2.083 mg/s), i.e. 100 sccm, while the text states 99 sccm = 2.06 mg/s (p.97; later 'limited to 100 sccm ... 2.06 mg/s', p.104). Anode flow ambiguity 1.0 %; possible feed-line leakage acknowledged (p.111).
derived_checks.global_efficiency: reported eta_G reproduces T^2/(2 (mdot_a + mdot_c) P_tot) with P_tot = P_a/(P_a/P_tot) to within 0.01-0.02 (Run 3: 0.266 vs 0.28), i.e. it includes cathode (Ar) flow and heater/keeper/magnet power (Eq. 5.2, 5.7). JAP 'total thrust efficiency 14-18 %' most likely the same quantity (verify).
derived_checks.anode_efficiency_class: reconstructed (T^2 / (2 mdot_a Vd Id), mdot_a 2.083 mg/s); Run 3 0.49 is implausible next to 0.13-0.23 and is a flagged unstable run

findings: E1 The only openly accessible primary source with per-point data is the 2020 MSc thesis (S2). The JAP paper (S1) is paywalled; the author-hosted copy is dead (404) and not archived. S1 very probably reports the same campaign.

E2 Per-point data exist: 13 (Vd, Id, Imag, cathode flow, pressure) points and 7 thrust points at 180-220 V, 2.06 mg/s N2. There are NO data at 225-275 V: cases/echt_n2.json's 200/225/250/275 V placeholders and the historical '250 V -> 24 mN, 690 W' calibration point (docs/HISTORY.md) are not supported by any openly accessible source (verify against S1 full text if it ever becomes accessible).

E3 The published B(z) is a flat plateau over the 46 mm iron walls (~4.7-8.6 cm), not exit-peaked; the Gaussian placeholder in cases/echt_n2.json is contradicted. Measured B exists at one coil current (2 A: plateau ~85.3 G, 12 % below FEMM). The quoted 130 G is FEMM at 3 A.
E4 Geometry is ambiguous at the radius level (100 mm = chamber OD); anode geometry/position unpublished.
E5 Thrust uncertainty is fit-only; the two published reductions differ by 6-18 %; 3 of 7 thrust runs are flagged strongly unstable; the thruster changed modes during calibration.
E6 Facility pressure is 0.8-2.5e-4 Torr, 5-10x higher than P5-N2 (1.1-2.1e-5 Torr) and I_d depends strongly on it (S2 Fig. 6.2: lowest I_d at lowest pressure). No facility correction is published.
E7 The cathode runs on argon at 7-36 % of the anode mass flow, a degraded BaO emitter; cathode flow co-varies with the best-performing points (Run 3: 0.74 mg/s Ar, lowest pressure, highest B).

E8 Table 6.2 Isp uses 2.083 mg/s while the text states 2.06 mg/s; 'global efficiency' includes cathode flow and heater/keeper/magnet power; the Table 6.1 'anode efficiency' is a power fraction. Fig. 6.2 colours the 180 V/3.0 A point as 200 V; figures show magnet currents 1.98/2.22/2.55 A vs table 2.0/2.2/2.6 A (minor).

conclusion.verdict: NOT USABLE AS AN INDEPENDENT, SCOREABLE VALIDATION DATASET WITHOUT FORCED ASSUMPTIONS. Usable at most as a supporting, pre-registered qualitative/semi-quantitative check (sustainment at 180-220 V, 2.06 mg/s; I_d magnitude and its decrease with coil current; thrust ~20-23 mN) with every forced assumption carried as a declared layer-1 nuisance, never as a promotion-deciding criterion on its own.
conclusion.independence: Independent of the P5-Xe selection (different thruster, lab, facility), so in principle a valid discriminator; the obstacle is observability, not independence.
forced_assumptions: A1 channel radii: 100 mm = channel OD (r 40/50 mm) vs BN piece OD (unknown wall thickness)
A2 anode axial position and the B(z) axis origin (exit at 86 vs 87.3 mm)
A3 B magnitude per run: FEMM interpolated in coil current, scaled (or not) by the single 2 A measured/FEMM ratio; 0.8 A extrapolated; radial position/component of the measured profile
A4 B(z) beyond 10.1-10.3 cm (plume region of the 1-D domain)
A5 cathode: neglect the argon cathode flow (7-36 % of anode mass) and choose a cathode coupling voltage/position
A6 facility: background pressure/ingestion model (0.8-2.5e-4 Torr, no published correction; comparison mode facility vs vacuum)
A7 thrust reduction reading (one-side vs averaged, 6-18 %) and a total thrust uncertainty (published +- are fit-only)
A8 plume divergence (no data) for any thrust comparison
A9 anode flow 2.06 vs 2.083 mg/s (1 %) and I_d uncertainty (rounding only)
A11 treatment of the strongly unstable runs (1, 3, 7) and of mode changes during calibration (I_d possibly not simultaneous with thrust)
conclusion.what_would_close_the_gaps: S1 full text (it may state radii, anode position, cathode position and a thrust uncertainty) - obtain legitimately only (library access or an openly licensed copy); no author contact under the standing rules.
